Article 14

(1) Women's empowerment in the economic field is implemented by means including:

a. facilitating women in efforts to improve the family economy;
b. providing capital assistance to women, especially migrant workers, women in remote areas, women as heads of households, and women victims of domestic violence; and
c. implementing home industry and non-agricultural industry development programs.
(2) The procedures for providing capital assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Paragraph 3

Provision of Services and Further Referral Handling Article 20

Provision of services and further referral handling as referred to in Article 17 letter b is intended for:

a. women victims of domestic violence; b. women victims of human trafficking crimes; c. women in emergency situations and special conditions; and
d. women victims of other acts of violence requiring Regency-level coordination.

Article 18

( 1 ) Prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 17 letter a is implemented by increasing family and community awareness.

( 2 ) Increasing family and community awareness as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted in an integrated and continuous manner in the form of socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling.

( 3 ) Socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out by the technical Regional Apparatus in charge, institutions, organizations, mass media, business community, academics, law enforcers, the community and Regional Technical Implementation Units in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality, hereinafter abbreviated as KG, is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender Analysis is a process that is systematically constructed to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access, and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as ARG, is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect the Child and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by a Child in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers body and soul and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disturbs the life and livelihood of the Child caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, foremost, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a Child by another party or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited for profit through sexual organs or other body organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and sexual abuse activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic Substances, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of the crime of pornography. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus, hereinafter abbreviated as HIV, is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce human immunity until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome, hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS, is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victim of Kidnapping is a Child who is taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of another person or to place the Child in a helpless state. 29. Child Victim of Sale is a Child who is transferred by a person or group of people to another party for a reward or other reason. 30.

Article 19

(1) In addition to prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 18, efforts to prevent violence against women are carried out by enhancing women's insight, knowledge, skills, and independence.

(2) Prevention of violence against women as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by means of:

a. enhancing informal education;
b. opening accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement, and social services; and
c. providing access to informal employment for women.

Article 17

Women's Protection is carried out by means of: a. prevention of violence against women;

b. provision of services and further referral handling; and

c. strengthening and development of women's protection service provider institutions.

Article 76

(1) Special Protection for Child Victims of Physical and/or Psychological Violence as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter i shall be carried out through efforts:

a. dissemination and socialization of the provisions of laws and regulations that protect Child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposing sanctions.
(2) Special Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided in the form of:
a. prevention;
b. assistance;
c. medical rehabilitation; and
d. Social Rehabilitation.
(3) Handling of Child Victims of Physical and/or Psychological Violence as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 78

(1) Monitoring as referred to in Article 76 paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out by:

a. observing and identifying the development of cases of physical and/or psychological violence against Children;
b. anticipating problems arising from cases of physical and/or psychological violence against Children; and
c. following up on cases of physical and/or psychological violence against Children.
(2) Reporting as referred to in Article 76 paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out periodically or at any time according to need.
(3) Imposing sanctions as referred to in Article 76 paragraph (1) letter b shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Child Victim of Trafficking is a Child who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, sheltering, sending, transfer, or receipt by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of the Child. 31. Child Victim of Physical Violence is a Child who experiences violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victim of Psychological Violence is a Child who experiences fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering. 33. Child Victim of Sexual Crime is a Child who experiences forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or undesired manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Child Victim of Terrorism Network is a Child who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by the crime of terrorism either as a child victim, child perpetrator, child of the perpetrator, and child witness. 35. Child with Disabilities is a Child who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term which in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victim of Maltreatment is a Child who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or the closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victim of Neglect is a Child who does not receive the fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child, resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Child with Deviant Social Behavior is a Child whose attitude and behavior does not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, shows an irresponsible attitude and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violates the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Child Who Is a Victim of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Parents' Condition is a Child who is given a negative social label based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing the Child with a bad stigma or view from labeling related to their parents' condition. 40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for the Child. 41. Educational Institution is an education unit as referred to in the laws and regulations concerning the national education system. 42. Counseling is a process carried out in the form of interviews to help Children understand themselves better, so that Children can overcome difficulties in adjusting themselves to various roles and relationships and find the right problem solving. 43. Social Assistance is a dynamic interaction between social workers and Children who need Special Protection to jointly face and solve social problems encountered. 44. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable Children to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life. 45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights, hereinafter abbreviated as PHA, is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child. 47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, either directly or indirectly based on differentiation of human beings on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, socio-cultural fields and other aspects of life. 48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical sexual exploitation, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or entity that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent to a child. 51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 52. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

Article 43

(1) Special Protection of Children from Minority and Isolated Groups so that they do not experience violence, discrimination, and other mistreatment as referred to in Article 41 shall be carried out through prevention efforts.

(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:

a. providing education to the community;and b. coordination with the Regency Government.
c. prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 118

To prevent the occurrence of stigmatization from labeling of Children related to their parents' condition, the Regency Government shall:

a. provide education to the Community and play an active role in eliminating stigma against Children who are labeled related to their parents' condition; b.provide space for Children who are labeled related to their parents' condition to obtain recreational activities; and
c. coordinate with service units that handle the protection of Children who are labeled related to their parents' condition in the event of potential violence and discrimination against Children in the Regency.

Paragraph 9

Child Victims of Physical and/or Psychological Violence

Article 120

( 1 ) The provision of service or advanced referral handling as referred to in Article 119 letter a shall be intended for child victims of violence who require Regency-level coordination.

( 2 ) The provision of service or referral handling as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented through the Regency-level PPA unit.

( 3 ) Further provisions regarding the duties, membership, and formation of the PPA unit as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 21

( 1 ) In addition to the provision of services and handling of service referrals as referred to in Article 20, the Regency Government is obligated to provide special services for:

a. women belonging to vulnerable and/or minority groups;
b. elderly women; and
c. women with special needs.
(2) Special services as referred to in paragraph (1) are provided in the form of:
a. facilitation in obtaining and enjoying their rights in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;
b. facilitation in access to economic resources and natural resources, social security, and basic public services; and
c. provision of specific needs for women in emergency situations and special conditions.
(3) Further provisions regarding special services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 141

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, Regional Regulation Number 6 of 2012 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children (Regional Gazette of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency Year 2012 Number 6), is revoked and declared invalid.

Article 82

(1) Education on reproductive health as referred to in Article 81 letter a shall be carried out so that Child Victims of Sexual Crimes:

a. have understanding to be protected from the risk of sexual crimes; and
b. know correct information about sexual education.
(2) Education on religious values and moral values as referred to in Article 81 letter a shall be carried out so that Child Victims of Sexual Crimes have strong faith and beliefs to overcome their problems.

Child Victims of Sexual Crimes

Article 46

(1) Monitoring as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be carried out by observation, identification, and recording to obtain data and information related to the condition of:

a. children who are Economically Exploited; or b. children who are Sexually Exploited.
(2) Monitoring of Children who are Economically Exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be carried out at economic center locations and outside economic centers.
(3) Monitoring of Children who are Sexually Exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out through supervision of:
a. practices of prostitution and solicitation in the environment;
b. locations suspected to be places of sexual exploitation of Children;
c. perpetrators suspected of sexually exploiting Children; and
d. raid actions to free Children from sexual exploitation.
(4) Monitoring and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Government.
(5) Reporting as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be prepared after monitoring of Children Who Are Economically and/or Sexually Exploited has been carried out.
(6) Imposition of sanctions as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality, hereinafter abbreviated as KG, is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender Analysis is a process that is systematically constructed to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access, and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as ARG, is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect the Child and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by a Child in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers body and soul and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disturbs the life and livelihood of the Child caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, foremost, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a Child by another party or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited for profit through sexual organs or other body organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and sexual abuse activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic Substances, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of the crime of pornography. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus, hereinafter abbreviated as HIV, is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce human immunity until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome, hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS, is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victim of Kidnapping is a Child who is taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of another person or to place the Child in a helpless state. 29. Child Victim of Sale is a Child who is transferred by a person or group of people to another party for a reward or other reason. 30.

Article 76

(1) Special Protection for Child Victims of Physical and/or Psychological Violence as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter i shall be carried out through efforts:

a. dissemination and socialization of the provisions of laws and regulations that protect Child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposing sanctions.
(2) Special Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided in the form of:
a. prevention;
b. assistance;
c. medical rehabilitation; and
d. Social Rehabilitation.

Paragraph 9

Child Victims of Physical and/or Psychological Violence

Child Victim of Trafficking is a Child who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, sheltering, sending, transfer, or receipt by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of the Child. 31. Child Victim of Physical Violence is a Child who experiences violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victim of Psychological Violence is a Child who experiences fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering. 33. Child Victim of Sexual Crime is a Child who experiences forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or undesired manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Child Victim of Terrorism Network is a Child who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by the crime of terrorism either as a child victim, child perpetrator, child of the perpetrator, and child witness. 35. Child with Disabilities is a Child who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term which in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victim of Maltreatment is a Child who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or the closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victim of Neglect is a Child who does not receive the fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child, resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Child with Deviant Social Behavior is a Child whose attitude and behavior does not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, shows an irresponsible attitude and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violates the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Child Who Is a Victim of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Parents' Condition is a Child who is given a negative social label based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing the Child with a bad stigma or view from labeling related to their parents' condition. 40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for the Child. 41. Educational Institution is an education unit as referred to in the laws and regulations concerning the national education system. 42. Counseling is a process carried out in the form of interviews to help Children understand themselves better, so that Children can overcome difficulties in adjusting themselves to various roles and relationships and find the right problem solving. 43. Social Assistance is a dynamic interaction between social workers and Children who need Special Protection to jointly face and solve social problems encountered. 44. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable Children to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life. 45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights, hereinafter abbreviated as PHA, is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child. 47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, either directly or indirectly based on differentiation of human beings on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, socio-cultural fields and other aspects of life. 48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical sexual exploitation, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or entity that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent to a child. 51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 52. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

Article 18

( 1 ) Prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 17 letter a is implemented by increasing family and community awareness.

( 2 ) Increasing family and community awareness as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted in an integrated and continuous manner in the form of socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling.

( 3 ) Socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out by the technical Regional Apparatus in charge, institutions, organizations, mass media, business community, academics, law enforcers, the community and Regional Technical Implementation Units in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 55

(1) Special Protection for Children who are Victims of Pornography as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter f is implemented through guidance, assistance, and social recovery, physical and mental health.

(2) Provisions regarding guidance, assistance, social recovery, physical and mental health as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 95

(1) Fulfillment of the rights of Child Victims of Terrorism Networks to care and psychological health recovery as referred to in Article 93 letter a is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) Medical rehabilitation as referred to in Article 93 letter b is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(3) Reeducation and Social Reintegration as referred to in Article 93 letter c are implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(4) Safety guarantees for the physical, mental, and social aspects of Child Victims of Terrorism Networks as referred to in Article 93 letter d are implemented by the District Government in accordance with its authority.

Article 19

(1) In addition to prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 18, efforts to prevent violence against women are carried out by enhancing women's insight, knowledge, skills, and independence.

Article 37

(1) Provision of legal aid and other assistance effectively as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter c is provided in the form of:

a. legal consultation, legal assistance, and defense in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;
b. provision of language interpreters for Children in legal processes including sign language interpreters for Children with Disabilities;
c. provision of information regarding the development of their case in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; and
d. provision of legal aid and other assistance effectively in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Implementation of recreational activities as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter d consists of daily free physical exercise activities in open spaces, daily entertainment activities, arts, or developing skills.
(3) Avoidance of arrest, detention, or imprisonment as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter g is carried out by taking into account the child's age, type of crime committed, threatened punishment, and criminal liability.
(4) Provision of justice before a Children's court that is objective, impartial, and in a hearing closed to the public as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter h is carried out by seeking a child-friendly court with infrastructure and facilities standards in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(5) Avoidance of publication of their identity as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter i is carried out by keeping confidential the name of the Child in Conflict with the Law, parents' names, address, face, and other things that can reveal the identity of the Child in Conflict with the Law.
(6) Provision of accompaniment by parents/guardians and persons trusted by the Child as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter j is carried out to help and provide support to the Child so they are ready to follow the process of investigation, prosecution, and examination in court proceedings.
(7) Provision of social advocacy as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter k is intended to protect and defend Children in Conflict with the Law provided in the form of awareness of rights and obligations, defense, and fulfillment of rights.
(8) Provision of health services as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter o is carried out in the form of promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of health.

Article 42

(1) The provision of facilities and infrastructure as referred to in Article 41 shall be carried out in the form of:

a. provision of culture-based public spaces, art and cultural centers, along with their equipment and training including places of worship;
b. provision of necessary facilities in providing services for Children from minority and isolated groups; and
c. providing accessibility needed by Children from minority and isolated groups to obtain fulfillment of basic needs.
(2) In the event that Children from minority and isolated groups experience trauma as a result of violence, discrimination and other mistreatment, they shall be provided with social rehabilitation, medical services, and/or mental health services.

Article 61

(1) Guidance and assistance as referred to in Article 53 paragraph (1) are carried out by the District Government in accordance with its authority.

(2) Social recovery, physical and mental health as referred to in Article 55 paragraph (1) are carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality, hereinafter abbreviated as KG, is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender Analysis is a process that is systematically constructed to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access, and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as ARG, is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect the Child and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by a Child in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers body and soul and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disturbs the life and livelihood of the Child caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, foremost, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a Child by another party or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited for profit through sexual organs or other body organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and sexual abuse activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic Substances, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of the crime of pornography. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus, hereinafter abbreviated as HIV, is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce human immunity until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome, hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS, is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victim of Kidnapping is a Child who is taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of another person or to place the Child in a helpless state. 29. Child Victim of Sale is a Child who is transferred by a person or group of people to another party for a reward or other reason. 30.

Article 18

( 1 ) Prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 17 letter a is implemented by increasing family and community awareness.

( 2 ) Increasing family and community awareness as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted in an integrated and continuous manner in the form of socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling.

( 3 ) Socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out by the technical Regional Apparatus in charge, institutions, organizations, mass media, business community, academics, law enforcers, the community and Regional Technical Implementation Units in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 14

(1) Women's empowerment in the economic field is implemented by means including:

a. facilitating women in efforts to improve the family economy;
b. providing capital assistance to women, especially migrant workers, women in remote areas, women as heads of households, and women victims of domestic violence; and
c. implementing home industry and non-agricultural industry development programs.
(2) The procedures for providing capital assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 19

(1) In addition to prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 18, efforts to prevent violence against women are carried out by enhancing women's insight, knowledge, skills, and independence.

(2) Prevention of violence against women as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by means of:

a. enhancing informal education;
b. opening accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement, and social services; and
c. providing access to informal employment for women.

Paragraph 3

Provision of Services and Further Referral Handling Article 20

Provision of services and further referral handling as referred to in Article 17 letter b is intended for:

a. women victims of domestic violence; b. women victims of human trafficking crimes; c. women in emergency situations and special conditions; and
d. women victims of other acts of violence requiring Regency-level coordination.

Article 17

Women's Protection is carried out by means of: a. prevention of violence against women;

b. provision of services and further referral handling; and

c. strengthening and development of women's protection service provider institutions.

Child Victim of Trafficking is a Child who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, sheltering, sending, transfer, or receipt by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of the Child. 31. Child Victim of Physical Violence is a Child who experiences violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victim of Psychological Violence is a Child who experiences fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering. 33. Child Victim of Sexual Crime is a Child who experiences forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or undesired manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Child Victim of Terrorism Network is a Child who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by the crime of terrorism either as a child victim, child perpetrator, child of the perpetrator, and child witness. 35. Child with Disabilities is a Child who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term which in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victim of Maltreatment is a Child who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or the closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victim of Neglect is a Child who does not receive the fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child, resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Child with Deviant Social Behavior is a Child whose attitude and behavior does not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, shows an irresponsible attitude and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violates the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Child Who Is a Victim of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Parents' Condition is a Child who is given a negative social label based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing the Child with a bad stigma or view from labeling related to their parents' condition. 40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for the Child. 41. Educational Institution is an education unit as referred to in the laws and regulations concerning the national education system. 42. Counseling is a process carried out in the form of interviews to help Children understand themselves better, so that Children can overcome difficulties in adjusting themselves to various roles and relationships and find the right problem solving. 43. Social Assistance is a dynamic interaction between social workers and Children who need Special Protection to jointly face and solve social problems encountered. 44. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable Children to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life. 45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights, hereinafter abbreviated as PHA, is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child. 47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, either directly or indirectly based on differentiation of human beings on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, socio-cultural fields and other aspects of life. 48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical sexual exploitation, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or entity that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent to a child. 51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 52. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

Paragraph 4

Children Who Are Economically and/or Sexually Exploited Article 44

Special Protection for Children Who Are Economically and/or Sexually Exploited as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter d shall be carried out through:

a. dissemination and/or socialization of provisions of laws and regulations related to the protection of Children Who Are Economically and/or Sexually Exploited;
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various companies, labor unions, non-governmental organizations, and the Community in the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children.

Article 46

(1) Monitoring as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be carried out by observation, identification, and recording to obtain data and information related to the condition of:

a. children who are Economically Exploited; or b. children who are Sexually Exploited.
(2) Monitoring of Children who are Economically Exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be carried out at economic center locations and outside economic centers.
(3) Monitoring of Children who are Sexually Exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out through supervision of:
a. practices of prostitution and solicitation in the environment;
b. locations suspected to be places of sexual exploitation of Children;
c. perpetrators suspected of sexually exploiting Children; and
d. raid actions to free Children from sexual exploitation.
(4) Monitoring and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Government.
(5) Reporting as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be prepared after monitoring of Children Who Are Economically and/or Sexually Exploited has been carried out.
(6) Imposition of sanctions as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 3

( 1 ) The Regency Government must guarantee the protection of women's rights.

( 2 ) Protection of women's rights as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:

a. formulation of gender-responsive regional policies;
b. institutionalization of PUG within the Regency Government;
c. women's empowerment in the field of education, field of health, field of employment, field of politics, field of law, field of economic culture and social in community organizations at the Regency level; and
d. strengthening and development of institutions providing women's empowerment services at the regency level.

Article 21

( 1 ) In addition to the provision of services and handling of service referrals as referred to in Article 20, the Regency Government is obligated to provide special services for:

a. women belonging to vulnerable and/or minority groups;
b. elderly women; and
c. women with special needs.
(2) Special services as referred to in paragraph (1) are provided in the form of:
a. facilitation in obtaining and enjoying their rights in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;
b. facilitation in access to economic resources and natural resources, social security, and basic public services; and
c. provision of specific needs for women in emergency situations and special conditions.
(3) Further provisions regarding special services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 2

( 1 ) Women's empowerment in the Regency is implemented through the protection of women's rights. ( 2 ) Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in order to fulfill women's rights in improving the quality of women's lives.

( 3 ) Women's rights as referred to in paragraph (2) must be guaranteed by the Regency Government. ( 4 ) Women's rights as referred to in paragraph (3) include the field of education, field of health, field of employment, field of politics, field of law, field of economic culture and social.

Article 141

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, Regional Regulation Number 6 of 2012 concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children (Regional Gazette of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency Year 2012 Number 6), is revoked and declared invalid.

Article 78

(1) Monitoring as referred to in Article 76 paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out by:

a. observing and identifying the development of cases of physical and/or psychological violence against Children;
b. anticipating problems arising from cases of physical and/or psychological violence against Children; and
c. following up on cases of physical and/or psychological violence against Children.
(2) Reporting as referred to in Article 76 paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out periodically or at any time according to need.
(3) Imposing sanctions as referred to in Article 76 paragraph (1) letter b shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 4

(1) The formulation of gender-responsive Regency policies as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter a serves as a guideline in the formulation of regional development plans.

(2) The formulation of development plans as referred to in paragraph (1) includes long-term plans, medium-term plans, and regional government work plans.

(3) The long-term development plan, medium-term plan, and regional government work plan as referred to in paragraph (2) must serve as a guideline for PD in the formulation of strategic plans and work plans in their respective work environments.

(4) The formulation of development plans as referred to in paragraph (3) is carried out through gender-responsive planning through gender analysis and ARG which contains a priority scale for the implementation of women's empowerment.

(5) The formulation of the priority scale for the implementation of women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (4) is based on the national level priority scale.

(6) The national level priority scale as referred to in paragraph (5) becomes an integral part of the regional development plan.

Article 22

(1) In order to provide services and further referral handling for women as referred to in Article 20, the Regency Government may establish:

a. a Regency-level Women and Children Protection (PPA) unit;
b. a task force; and/or
c. a task unit.
(2) The PPA unit, task force, and/or task unit as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be established by Regent Regulation.
(3) Further provisions regarding the duties, membership, procedures and/or work task unit of the PPA unit as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 30

( 1 ) Parents are obligated and responsible to: a. care for, nurture, educate, and protect children;

b. develop children according to their abilities, talents, and interests; and

c. prevent marriage at child age.

(2) In the event that parents are absent, or their whereabouts are unknown, or for any reason, cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1) may transfer to the family, which shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 8

Women's empowerment in the field of education, field of health, field of employment, field of politics, field of law, field of economic culture and social in community organizations at the Regency level as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter c is part of temporary special policies provided by the Regency Government.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu. 4. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Analysis is a process that is systematically constructed to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access, and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as ARG, is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect the Child and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by a Child in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers body and soul and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disturbs the life and livelihood of the Child caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, foremost, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a Child by another party or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited for profit through sexual organs or other body organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and sexual abuse activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic Substances, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of the crime of pornography. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus, hereinafter abbreviated as HIV, is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce human immunity until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome, hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS, is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victim of Kidnapping is a Child who is taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of another person or to place the Child in a helpless state. 29. Child Victim of Sale is a Child who is transferred by a person or group of people to another party for a reward or other reason. 30.

Paragraph 4

Children Who Are Economically and/or Sexually Exploited Article 44

Special Protection for Children Who Are Economically and/or Sexually Exploited as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter d shall be carried out through:

a. dissemination and/or socialization of provisions of laws and regulations related to the protection of Children Who Are Economically and/or Sexually Exploited;
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions; and
c. involvement of various companies, labor unions, non-governmental organizations, and the Community in the elimination of economic and/or sexual exploitation of Children.

Article 46

(1) Monitoring as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be carried out by observation, identification, and recording to obtain data and information related to the condition of:

a. children who are Economically Exploited; or b. children who are Sexually Exploited.
(2) Monitoring of Children who are Economically Exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be carried out at economic center locations and outside economic centers.
(3) Monitoring of Children who are Sexually Exploited as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out through supervision of:
a. practices of prostitution and solicitation in the environment;
b. locations suspected to be places of sexual exploitation of Children;
c. perpetrators suspected of sexually exploiting Children; and
d. raid actions to free Children from sexual exploitation.
(4) Monitoring and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regency Government.
(5) Reporting as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be prepared after monitoring of Children Who Are Economically and/or Sexually Exploited has been carried out.
(6) Imposition of sanctions as referred to in Article 44 letter b shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Child Victim of Trafficking is a Child who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, sheltering, sending, transfer, or receipt by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of the Child. 31. Child Victim of Physical Violence is a Child who experiences violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victim of Psychological Violence is a Child who experiences fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering. 33. Child Victim of Sexual Crime is a Child who experiences forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or undesired manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Child Victim of Terrorism Network is a Child who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by the crime of terrorism either as a child victim, child perpetrator, child of the perpetrator, and child witness. 35. Child with Disabilities is a Child who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term which in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victim of Maltreatment is a Child who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or the closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victim of Neglect is a Child who does not receive the fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child, resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Child with Deviant Social Behavior is a Child whose attitude and behavior does not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, shows an irresponsible attitude and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violates the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Child Who Is a Victim of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Parents' Condition is a Child who is given a negative social label based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing the Child with a bad stigma or view from labeling related to their parents' condition. 40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for the Child. 41. Educational Institution is an education unit as referred to in the laws and regulations concerning the national education system. 42. Counseling is a process carried out in the form of interviews to help Children understand themselves better, so that Children can overcome difficulties in adjusting themselves to various roles and relationships and find the right problem solving. 43. Social Assistance is a dynamic interaction between social workers and Children who need Special Protection to jointly face and solve social problems encountered. 44. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable Children to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life. 45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights, hereinafter abbreviated as PHA, is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child. 47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, either directly or indirectly based on differentiation of human beings on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, socio-cultural fields and other aspects of life. 48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical sexual exploitation, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or entity that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent to a child. 51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 52. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality, hereinafter abbreviated as KG, is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender Analysis is a process that is systematically constructed to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access, and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as ARG, is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect the Child and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by a Child in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers body and soul and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disturbs the life and livelihood of the Child caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, foremost, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a Child by another party or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited for profit through sexual organs or other body organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and sexual abuse activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic Substances, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of the crime of pornography. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus, hereinafter abbreviated as HIV, is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce human immunity until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome, hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS, is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victim of Kidnapping is a Child who is taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of another person or to place the Child in a helpless state. 29. Child Victim of Sale is a Child who is transferred by a person or group of people to another party for a reward or other reason. 30.
