Child Victim of Trafficking is a Child who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, sheltering, sending, transfer, or receipt by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of the Child. 31. Child Victim of Physical Violence is a Child who experiences violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victim of Psychological Violence is a Child who experiences fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering. 33. Child Victim of Sexual Crime is a Child who experiences forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or undesired manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Child Victim of Terrorism Network is a Child who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by the crime of terrorism either as a child victim, child perpetrator, child of the perpetrator, and child witness. 35. Child with Disabilities is a Child who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term which in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victim of Maltreatment is a Child who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or the closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victim of Neglect is a Child who does not receive the fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child, resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Child with Deviant Social Behavior is a Child whose attitude and behavior does not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, shows an irresponsible attitude and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violates the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Child Who Is a Victim of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Parents' Condition is a Child who is given a negative social label based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing the Child with a bad stigma or view from labeling related to their parents' condition. 40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for the Child. 41. Educational Institution is an education unit as referred to in the laws and regulations concerning the national education system. 42. Counseling is a process carried out in the form of interviews to help Children understand themselves better, so that Children can overcome difficulties in adjusting themselves to various roles and relationships and find the right problem solving. 43. Social Assistance is a dynamic interaction between social workers and Children who need Special Protection to jointly face and solve social problems encountered. 44. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable Children to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life. 45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights, hereinafter abbreviated as PHA, is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child. 47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, either directly or indirectly based on differentiation of human beings on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, socio-cultural fields and other aspects of life. 48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical sexual exploitation, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or entity that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent to a child. 51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 52. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

Article 4

(1) The formulation of gender-responsive Regency policies as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2) letter a serves as a guideline in the formulation of regional development plans.

(2) The formulation of development plans as referred to in paragraph (1) includes long-term plans, medium-term plans, and regional government work plans.

(3) The long-term development plan, medium-term plan, and regional government work plan as referred to in paragraph (2) must serve as a guideline for PD in the formulation of strategic plans and work plans in their respective work environments.

(4) The formulation of development plans as referred to in paragraph (3) is carried out through gender-responsive planning through gender analysis and ARG which contains a priority scale for the implementation of women's empowerment.

(5) The formulation of the priority scale for the implementation of women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (4) is based on the national level priority scale.

(6) The national level priority scale as referred to in paragraph (5) becomes an integral part of the regional development plan.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occurs as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality, hereinafter abbreviated as KG, is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender Analysis is a process that is systematically constructed to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access, and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as ARG, is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over economic, political, social, and cultural resources, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect the Child and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by a Child in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers body and soul and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger their body and life in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in an environmental situation that threatens and disturbs the life and livelihood of the Child caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, foremost, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, ethnicities, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical, sexual, reproductive organ exploitation, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a Child by another party or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited for profit through sexual organs or other body organs of the Child, including but not limited to all prostitution and sexual abuse activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic Substances, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of the crime of pornography. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus, hereinafter abbreviated as HIV, is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce human immunity until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome, hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS, is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victim of Kidnapping is a Child who is taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of another person or to place the Child in a helpless state. 29. Child Victim of Sale is a Child who is transferred by a person or group of people to another party for a reward or other reason. 30.

CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 42

(1) The provision of facilities and infrastructure as referred to in Article 41 shall be carried out in the form of:

a. provision of culture-based public spaces, art and cultural centers, along with their equipment and training including places of worship;
b. provision of necessary facilities in providing services for Children from minority and isolated groups; and
c. providing accessibility needed by Children from minority and isolated groups to obtain fulfillment of basic needs.
(2) In the event that Children from minority and isolated groups experience trauma as a result of violence, discrimination and other mistreatment, they shall be provided with social rehabilitation, medical services, and/or mental health services.

Article 95

(1) Fulfillment of the rights of Child Victims of Terrorism Networks to care and psychological health recovery as referred to in Article 93 letter a is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) Medical rehabilitation as referred to in Article 93 letter b is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(3) Reeducation and Social Reintegration as referred to in Article 93 letter c are implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(4) Safety guarantees for the physical, mental, and social aspects of Child Victims of Terrorism Networks as referred to in Article 93 letter d are implemented by the District Government in accordance with its authority.

Paragraph 12

Children with Disabilities

Child Victim of Trafficking is a Child who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, sheltering, sending, transfer, or receipt by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of the Child. 31. Child Victim of Physical Violence is a Child who experiences violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victim of Psychological Violence is a Child who experiences fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, a sense of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering. 33. Child Victim of Sexual Crime is a Child who experiences forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or undesired manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Child Victim of Terrorism Network is a Child who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by the crime of terrorism either as a child victim, child perpetrator, child of the perpetrator, and child witness. 35. Child with Disabilities is a Child who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term which in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victim of Maltreatment is a Child who is threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, treated wrongly or improperly in the family environment or the closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victim of Neglect is a Child who does not receive the fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child, resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Child with Deviant Social Behavior is a Child whose attitude and behavior does not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, shows an irresponsible attitude and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violates the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Child Who Is a Victim of Stigmatization from Labeling related to Parents' Condition is a Child who is given a negative social label based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing the Child with a bad stigma or view from labeling related to their parents' condition. 40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for the Child. 41. Educational Institution is an education unit as referred to in the laws and regulations concerning the national education system. 42. Counseling is a process carried out in the form of interviews to help Children understand themselves better, so that Children can overcome difficulties in adjusting themselves to various roles and relationships and find the right problem solving. 43. Social Assistance is a dynamic interaction between social workers and Children who need Special Protection to jointly face and solve social problems encountered. 44. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable Children to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life. 45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights, hereinafter abbreviated as PHA, is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child. 47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, either directly or indirectly based on differentiation of human beings on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, socio-cultural fields and other aspects of life. 48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim that includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, physical sexual exploitation, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or entity that in reality exercises parental authority as a parent to a child. 51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 52. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

CHAPTER VI

COORDINATION AND COOPERATION

Article 87

(1) Education about reproductive health, religious values, and moral values as referred to in Article 81 letter a is implemented by the District Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) Social Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 83 letter b is implemented by the District Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(3) Psychosocial assistance during treatment until recovery as referred to in Article 81 letter c is implemented by the District Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(4) Provision of protection and assistance at every level of examination starting from investigation, prosecution, up to examination at court hearings as referred to in Article 81 letter d is implemented by the District Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(5) Implementation of Special Protection as referred to in Article 86 is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 133

(1) The Regent shall be obliged to provide guidance on the organization of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) The implementation of guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers women's empowerment and child protection affairs.

(3) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall include:

a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(4) Supervision shall be implemented in the form of:
a. monitoring; and
b. evaluation.
(5) In implementing guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Apparatus that administers women's empowerment and child protection affairs may cooperate and coordinate with other Regional Apparatus within the Regency Government or other agencies/institutions related to the Regency.

Article 18

( 1 ) Prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 17 letter a is implemented by increasing family and community awareness.

( 2 ) Increasing family and community awareness as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted in an integrated and continuous manner in the form of socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling.

( 3 ) Socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out by the technical Regional Apparatus in charge, institutions, organizations, mass media, business community, academics, law enforcers, the community and Regional Technical Implementation Units in accordance with their duties and functions.

Article 25

(1) Coordination of child-friendly regency development as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (1) letter c is implemented to encourage the acceleration of the realization of a Child-Friendly Regency.

(2) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by related agencies in accordance with their main duties and functions.

(3) Further provisions regarding the form and procedures for coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 117

Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance as referred to in Article 113 shall be carried out by the Regency Government in accordance with its duties, functions, and authorities.

Article 69

(1) Supervision efforts as referred to in Article 63 are carried out by the District Government in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 64 and Treatment, care, and rehabilitation as referred to in Article 65 through Article 67 are carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 135

(1) In addition to the Regional Apparatus that administers women's empowerment and child protection affairs, to ensure the effectiveness of implementing women's empowerment and child protection in the Regency, every Regional Apparatus shall be obliged to conduct supervision in the form of monitoring and evaluation.

(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in tiers in accordance with their respective authorities.

(3) The results of monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be announced to the public.
